team_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me invite a new teammate to our {{vendor}} workspace with the correct access level. Before starting, ask me for any of the following if not already known: the teammate's email address, the {{vendor}} workspace/organization name or URL, the intended access level (e.g., full member, guest/limited access, or admin), and whether they should be added to any specific channels (public or private) upon joining.

Once you have this information, using my configured credentials, log into the {{vendor}} admin or workspace settings area and:
1. Locate the member invitation or 'invite people' section.
2. Enter the teammate's email address.
3. Set their access level according to my instructions — if they are an external partner or collaborator, use a guest account or limited-access role rather than full membership; if they are a full internal teammate, assign standard member access (or admin, only if explicitly requested).
4. If specific channels were named, add the invite to those channels with appropriate membership controls (private channels should restrict visibility to only the intended members).
5. Send the invite.

After sending, confirm the invite appears in the workspace's pending invitations list with the correct email, role, and channel assignments.

Done looks like: the teammate has a pending or accepted invite in {{vendor}} with the correct access level (guest/limited or full member) and correct channel memberships as specified.

Report back to me with: the teammate's email, the access level granted, any channels they were added to, and the current invite status (pending/accepted). If the {{vendor}} interface requires any confirmation or approval step that only an account owner can complete, note that this remains a human step and stop there.

team_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me track the status of a teammate invitation I sent as part of onboarding a new org member. The actual acceptance of the invite email and account setup (name, password, etc.) must be completed by the invited teammate themselves on their own timeline — this remains a human step and you cannot perform it or fill it in on their behalf.

What I need from you: please ask me for (1) the name/email of the invited teammate, (2) the platform or tool they were invited to (e.g., our project management tool, cloud provider, CRM, etc.), and (3) where I can check invite status (admin/team/members dashboard URL or app name) if I haven't already provided it.

Once you have this, your job is to:
1. Log into the relevant admin dashboard using my configured credentials.
2. Navigate to the team/members management section and locate the invited teammate's entry.
3. Check and report their current invite status (e.g., "Pending", "Accepted", "Expired") and, if visible, the access level assigned to them.
4. If the invite shows as expired or stuck in pending for an unusually long time, prepare a draft reminder message (email or chat) I could send to nudge them, but do not send it — just have it ready for me to review.
5. Note the date/time you checked so I can track how long the invite has been outstanding.

Done looks like: you've confirmed the current status of the invite and reported back clearly whether it's still pending or has been accepted, along with the assigned access level if visible, plus a draft reminder ready if needed. Report back with the status, timestamp checked, and any draft text prepared. Do not attempt to accept the invite or set up credentials on the teammate's behalf — only they can do that.

team_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me complete a teammate onboarding step in {{vendor}}, our team-chat tool. A new member has already been invited to the organization and had their access level set. Your job now is to add them to the right channels and confirm their access is correct.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in your configured credentials or context, specifically:
1. The new teammate's name or account identifier in {{vendor}}.
2. The list of channels they should join (public and/or private), based on their team or role.
3. Whether they need guest/external-partner-level access to any shared channels, or full internal member access.

Once you have this information:
- Using your configured credentials, add the teammate to each specified public and private channel via the {{vendor}} dashboard or API, respecting membership controls (e.g., request-to-join or admin-approval flows for private channels).
- If any channels involve external collaboration, confirm the teammate is added with the correct guest or limited-access permission level rather than full internal access.
- After adding them, verify their channel membership list matches what was requested, and confirm their permission level in each channel (member, guest, admin, etc.) is correct.
- If {{vendor}} provides audit logs, check that the addition actions are logged correctly for the platform-engineer's audit trail.

Done looks like: the teammate is a confirmed member of every listed channel, with the correct access level (internal or guest) in each, and no channel membership or permission mismatches remain.

Report back to me with: the teammate's name, the final list of channels they were added to, their access level in each, any channels that required special (guest/external) handling, and confirmation that audit logging (if applicable) captured these changes. Flag any channel where you could not confirm membership or permissions so I can follow up manually.
